node.title: Re^2: Detecting last line and blank line
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
[Anonymous Monk]: [doc://eof] is indeed useful, and just to add two points to what [davido] wrote, there are two peculiarities when it is used in [doc://perlop#I/O-Operators|while (<>)] loops, including the implicit ones from the [doc://perlrun|-n and -p] command line switches. First, eof with and without empty parentheses is different - from its docs:

In a while (<>) loop, eof or eof(ARGV) can be used to detect the end of each file, whereas eof() will detect the end of the very last file only.

Second, [davido]'s code example uses the line counter [doc://$.], which does not get reset for each file in a while (<>) loop. To do that, you need [doc://close] [doc://perlvar#ARGV] explicitly, that is:

while (<>) { # your code here } continue { close ARGV if eof; # Not eof()! }

This is normally done in a [doc://continue] block because that way, it will still be executed even if you use [doc://next] inside the loop.

As for blank lines, I like to use next unless /\S/; to skip lines that contain only whitespace. That doesn't exactly meet your "0 characters" requirement - as [LanX] [id://1202898|said], use eq to compare the line to "" after [doc://chomp] (or to "\n" before).

Although you don't say why you need to detect blank lines and the last line, note that setting [doc://$/|$/="";] means files will be read in "paragraph mode", that is, records will be separated by one or more blank lines.
